scope: Coverage census plus live primary-source component review. Castor, Spica, Nunki and Menkalinan literature updates are adopted; this is not a claim of exhaustive publication coverage for every catalog star.

sources.finding: The Lohrmann Observatory announcement gives 2 December 2026 as the planned DR4 release. DR3 remains the appropriate full public Gaia release at this review date. A retrieval date in October 2026 does not make the underlying DR3 measurements a 2026 release.
sources.releaseStatus: DR4 upcoming; do not import pre-release expectations as measurements. ESA's direct DR4 overview failed to load in the research tool; the project-partner observatory announcement was accessible.

sources.finding: Sections I and IV.2 identify Castor C as YY Gem, itself a double-lined eclipsing binary: Castor has six stars. Existing Aa/Ab/Ba/Bb masses and Aa/Ba radii already use this paper. Section IV.1 gives a preferred 290 Myr model age from Aa, with a Ba-radius discrepancy; this is a shared, model-dependent age, not six independent age measurements. The paper points to dedicated YY Gem studies for individual C-component properties.

Table 7 resolves the close binary: primary/secondary masses 11.43 +/- 1.15 and 7.21 +/- 0.75 solar masses; radii 7.47 +/- 0.54 and 3.74 +/- 0.53 solar radii; temperatures 25300 +/- 500 and 20900 +/- 800 K; log10 luminosities 4.312 +/- 0.095 and 3.353 +/- 0.181. The abstract gives a model system age of 12.5 +/- 1 Myr. Later papers must be compared before choosing adopted values. None of these individual values belongs on an unresolved Aab row.

March 2026 study of Sigma Sagittarii/Nunki Aa/Ab. Table 2 gives a 134.779 +/- 0.025 day orbit and TOTAL dynamical mass 14.6 +/- 1.8 solar masses, with 2.3-97.7 percentile bounds (not one sigma). Section 4.1 prefers approximate individual isochrone masses 6.5 and 6.3 solar masses, referring to the 2025 study; section 3.4 estimates 18.5 kK from combined spectra. Review these against the current dwarf-sequence primary estimate and missing component masses; do not copy the total mass to either star or assume two independent temperature measurements.

September 2026 joint interferometry/RV/photometry solution. Adopt Table 8 masses/radii with profile-likelihood uncertainties, retain the inherited primary temperature calibration, and derive the secondary temperature conditionally from the new ratio. Earlier 2007 values and their evidence survive.

True individual masses in Table 2 and volume-equivalent radii in section V.1 adopted for YY Gem A/B, explicitly mapped to Castor Ca/Cb. The common 3800 K atmosphere parameter retains its adopted-model scope.

Updated B-star interferometry study checked for Spica multiplicity. It does not provide a replacement resolved binary dynamical solution; approximate flux-derived mass ratios are not substituted for the individual 2016 masses.
